The Bend in the Road (heading at line 10504, the last chapter of thirty-eight), the text runs “When I left Queen's my future seemed to stretch out before me like a straight road. I thought I could see along it for many a milestone. Now there is a bend in it. I don't know what lies around the bend, but I'm going to believe that the best does. It has a fascination of its own, that bend, Marilla.” Word for word, curly apostrophes throughout, no straight quote. Speaker and addressee are fixed by the surrounding text: Anne has just said “I'm not going to Redmond; and I am going to stay here and teach”, and four lines after the quotation Marilla answers “I don't feel as if I ought to let you give it up,” said Marilla, referring to the scholarship. So the speaker parenthesis (Anne Shirley) is right and the locator's account of the scene is right; the only looseness is that the scholarship is the Avery, which would have paid for Redmond, and that detail lives in the evidence, not in the printed source line.
